entries.note: PMID 19846789 / PNAS 106:18825 resolves. Quote is the abstract sentence truncated at 32 words ('Cl(-)' rendered as 'Cl−'). No patient data in 2009, so untested is right. Abstract-level.

PMID 21083385, NEJM 363:1991 (Nov 2010). Abstract itself states the in-vitro premise then NPD/sweat chloride, so comparison_stated=true holds (qualitative). registry_date should be 2012-10-05 (NCT00457821 results first posted), not null.

Verified in the ClinPharm review text (p.53): 'proposed dose and dosing regimen is based on exposure-response analysis of dose finding study (vx06-770-101)'; EC50 28/48 ng/mL on p.50; no in-vitro EC50 vs exposure comparison anywhere in the review. Untested stands.

PMID 39755444 resolves (J Cyst Fibros 24:246, print 2025; not OA, abstract only). It correlates sweat chloride with HBE chloride current across healthy/carriers/treated patients: a PD-to-PD calibration, no exposure or occupancy target tested. Not a dose comparison; cell stays untested. Re-file as engagement magnitude support.
Closing sentence of the Van Goor 2009 abstract, verbatim. Untested correct.

PMID 22047557, NEJM 365:1663 (Nov 2011). Abstract makes no in-vitro reference, so comparison_stated=false is honest; full text not reachable (PMC captcha, not in Europe PMC). Status rests on juxtaposition with Van Goor 2009; first in-document comparison is the FDA 2012 review (pp.77-78). registry_date NCT00909532 = 2012-08-21.

Both quotes verified verbatim in the review PDF (F508del/F508del result §2.6.3 p.33; HBE 'limited' flag §3.1.1 p.77). But the brief's neg needs a drug of the class that failed; this is a correct negative for a genotype outside the context's population (modulator-responsive). Keep same; neg not met. Primary trial paper is Flume 2012 Chest doi:10.1378/chest.11-2672 ('difference ... 1.7% (P = .15)'), NCT00953706 results posted 2012-08-21.

s001 label text extracted: 'Revised: August 2012'; quote verbatim in §13.2 ('This finding has not been observed in older animals' follows). §5 has only 5.1 Transaminase and 5.2 CYP3A inducers, so no warning yet. Original Jan-2012 label not re-checked by me.

s014 label 'Revised: 12/2014'; §5.3 verbatim, continuing 'Although other risk factors were present in some cases (such as corticosteroid use and/or exposure to radiation), a possible risk attributable to KALYDECO cannot be excluded.' An unattributed signal with named confounders is not a patient result that agrees with the prediction; scoring it same over-credits animal tox. Keep the entry as an unresolved-signal note; no status change. Which 2014 supplement introduced §5.3 still unpinned; 2013 labels not checked by me.

missing: registry_date is mandatory under brief v2 rule 7 but every entry is null. From ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (resultsFirstPostDate): NCT00457821 (Accurso phase 2) 2012-10-05; NCT00909532 (STRIVE) 2012-08-21; NCT00909727 (ENVISION) 2012-08-21; NCT00953706 (DISCOVER / Study 104, F508del homozygous) 2012-08-21.

Flume 2012 Chest (doi:10.1378/chest.11-2672, PMID 22383668) is the primary publication of Study 104 and is now verified: 'The difference in the change of FEV1 % predicted from baseline through week 16 (primary end point) between the ivacaftor and placebo groups was 1.7% (P = .15)' and 'a CFTR potentiator alone is not an effective therapeutic approach for patients who have CF and are homozygous for F508del-CFTR.' Cite it beside the FDA review wherever the F508del/F508del negative is kept.

The FDA's own caveat on the model belongs in the dose/efficacy notes: 2014 label §12.2 'In vitro responses do not necessarily correspond to in vivo pharmacodynamic response or clinical benefit.' and §14 (2012 and 2014 labels) 'There was no direct correlation between decrease in sweat chloride levels and improvement in lung function (FEV1).' Durmowicz 2013 Chest (doi:10.1378/chest.12-1430) makes the same point from the FDA dose-finding analysis; it undercuts any PD-scale dose claim such as Zemanick 2025.

Corrector-era magnitude comparisons (lumacaftor/ivacaftor, Wainwright 2015 doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1409547; elexacaftor triple, Keating 2018 / Middleton 2019) would populate magnitude for efficacy without changing status; not verified within this check's budget.

SEED COMPARISON (contexts/cf-cftr.json vs draft), cells that differ: (1) engagement same: seed 2011 (Ramsey, sweat chloride -48 mmol/L) vs draft 2010 (Accurso, -59.5 mmol/L, P=0.02 vs placebo). Draft better supported: earlier published comparison whose abstract itself states the in-vitro premise; rule 5 dates by publication (registry posting 2012-10-05 is later still). (2) dose: seed untested only (model 'rat cells carrying each CFTR mutation' = FRT; note that the label says in-vitro gain does not correlate with response, which I verified in label §12.2) vs draft untested 2009 then same 2025 (Zemanick). Seed's status better supported (Zemanick is PD-PD calibration, not an exposure target); the draft's untested entry is the better-sourced one (FDA exposure-response dose basis verified, HBE EC50 never compared with exposure). Neither FRT nor HBE was relied on for dose. (3) efficacy: seed untested 2009 (FRT) then same 2017 (Durmowicz 2018, 23-mutation label expansion on in-vitro data) vs draft untested 2009 (HBE), same 2011 (Ramsey), neg 2012 (FDA review). Draft better supported for same: the seed's 2017 entry is regulatory reliance on the model 'in lieu of a clinical trial' (its own abstract), i.e. no patient-outcome comparison (rule 5 failure), its year is the label action not the print year (Ann ATS Jan 2018; rule-3 failure), and it is a perspective by FDA staff rather than a comparison. Draft's neg should revert to same (efficacy index 3 above). (4) safety: seed empty vs draft untested 2012 then same 2014 (juvenile-rat cataracts / pediatric lens opacities). Draft better supported: the seed missed a real labelled model-vs-patient pairing; I would keep the 2014 label as an unresolved signal rather than same. (5) Not a status/year difference: population wording ('variants' vs 'genotype'), mechanism label, and the efficacy model (FRT vs HBE). The FDA review relies on both (FRT Fig 30, HBE Fig 31); HBE matches Van Goor 2009's title and the G551D pivotal rationale, FRT the 2017 expansion; the draft's choice is defensible.
rule_questions: neg and genotype-level failure: the rule says 'a drug of this class that went on to fail in patients'. Here the same approved drug failed in a genotype (F508del/F508del) the HBE model flagged, and that genotype sits outside the context's population by construction. Is a correct negative prediction for an excluded population a neg for this context, a same for a separate context (CF x F508del homozygous x potentiator monotherapy), or neither? I scored it as not meeting neg.

dose vs PD-scale calibration: does a published correlation of a model PD readout (HBE chloride current) with a patient PD readout (sweat chloride) satisfy 'the model's exposure/occupancy target held in patients'? I read dose as exposure/occupancy only and filed the PD-PD correlation under engagement magnitude; the brief should say so explicitly.

safety with an unattributed patient signal: a label that pairs an animal finding with patient case reports but says the risk 'cannot be excluded' is a published comparison with no adjudicated patient result. untested denies the comparison exists; same asserts agreement the source does not claim. The brief needs a 'compared, unresolved' handling (or a requirement that source_calls_it = match for same).

opening a dose strip when no preclinical model was relied on for dose: ivacaftor's dose came from clinical exposure-response, so under 'best model = the model the class relied on' the dose cell arguably has no model and should be an empty list rather than untested with the engagement model's EC50.

juxtaposed sources: v2 made comparison_stated a fact field, but rule 1 still says the source must 'make the comparison'. Efficacy same in 2011 (Ramsey) rests on juxtaposition with Van Goor 2009; the first in-document comparison is the FDA 2012 review. The brief should state whether a juxtaposed pair can set the year.
